newsitem.title: FRANCE: Three unions open to France Telecom sale.
newsitem.headline: Three unions open to France Telecom sale.

text.p: The CFTC union said on Tuesday it would give qualified backing if a new Socialist-led government decided on partial privatisation of France Telecom.

The CFTC said in a statement it wanted guarantees for a high quality public service, that the employees should retain civil service status and that France Telecom should have the resources to meet the entry of new operators from January 1998.

If the state "confirms its desire for the partial privatisation for France Telecom, the CFTC...will pursue its actions so that the maximum of employees will have the opportunity to become employee shareholders," it said.
Marc Blondel, leader of the Force Ouvriere union, also said he was not opposed to such a move if it proved necessary.
"I am for the public sector in a general way," he said.

"(But) There is the special case for telecommunications. And it is certain that in telecommunications, the important thing is that everyone should have access to modern telecoms. I would say it is a democratic objective," he told Reuters.
The state faced problems financing modern telecom services.
"If it were possible, I would like (France Telecom) to remain 100 percent under state control but it is not certain, it is not as simple as that," he said.
CFDT union leader Nicole Notat said earlier on Tuesday she was not hostile to a partial privatisation of France Telecom as long as the state maintained a high quality public service.
A France Telecom spokesman said the sale of the state's minority stake in the operator was suspended until the new government decides on its policy.

The centre-right, which lost power to the left in Sunday's parliamentary election, had planned the sale of between 30-35 percent of the capital of France Telecom, whose total value has been estimated at between 160-210 billion francs.

The only high-profile national trade union outrightly opposed to a France Telecom stake sale is the Communist-led CGT, whose leader Louis Viannet said on Tuesday he wanted the sale plan, and privatisations generally, scrapped.
